zodiacs.name: Aries
zodiacs.origin: Aries is derived from the Latin word for 'ram'. In Greek mythology, it represents the golden ram whose fleece was sought by Jason and the Argonauts. The constellation has been recognized since ancient Babylonian times.

zodiacs.name: Taurus
zodiacs.origin: Taurus represents the bull in various mythologies. In Greek myth, it's associated with Zeus who transformed into a bull to abduct Europa. The constellation has been observed since ancient times and represents strength and fertility.

zodiacs.name: Gemini
zodiacs.origin: Gemini represents the twins Castor and Pollux from Greek mythology. They were known for their brotherly love and were placed in the sky as a constellation. The sign symbolizes duality and communication.

zodiacs.name: Cancer
zodiacs.origin: Cancer is represented by the crab that Hera sent to distract Hercules during his battle with the Hydra. Though the crab was crushed, Hera honored its sacrifice by placing it among the stars.

zodiacs.name: Leo
zodiacs.origin: Leo represents the Nemean Lion that Hercules slayed as his first labor. The lion's golden hide was impervious to weapons, and after defeating it, Zeus placed the lion among the stars to honor its strength.

zodiacs.name: Virgo
zodiacs.origin: Virgo is often associated with Persephone or Astraea, goddess of justice, who fled to the heavens during the decline of the Golden Age. The constellation represents purity, harvest, and analytical thinking.

zodiacs.name: Libra
zodiacs.origin: Libra represents the scales of justice held by Astraea, goddess of justice. It's the only zodiac sign represented by an inanimate object, symbolizing balance, harmony, and fairness in all aspects of life.

zodiacs.name: Scorpio
zodiacs.origin: Scorpio represents the scorpion sent by Gaia to kill Orion, the great hunter who boasted he could kill any creature. Both were placed in the sky, with Scorpio rising as Orion sets, continuing their eternal chase.

zodiacs.name: Sagittarius
zodiacs.origin: Sagittarius is represented by the centaur archer, often identified with Chiron, the wise centaur who taught heroes. The constellation symbolizes the pursuit of knowledge, adventure, and higher learning.

zodiacs.name: Capricorn
zodiacs.origin: Capricorn represents the sea-goat, associated with the god Pan who transformed into a goat-fish to escape the monster Typhon. It symbolizes ambition, discipline, and the ability to navigate both earthly and emotional realms.

zodiacs.name: Aquarius
zodiacs.origin: Aquarius represents Ganymede, the cup-bearer to the gods, or the Egyptian god of the Nile flood. Despite being the 'water bearer,' it's an air sign, symbolizing the flow of ideas and humanitarian ideals.

zodiacs.name: Pisces
zodiacs.origin: Pisces represents two fish swimming in opposite directions, symbolizing the dual nature of this sign. In mythology, they represent Aphrodite and Eros who transformed into fish to escape the monster Typhon.
